purpose: Rates whether a DECLARED authenticator set and session policy reach a DECLARED target level of a caller-supplied, versioned authentication assurance framework -- never a hardcoded framework such as NIST SP 800-63B or the eIDAS levels of assurance. This is the authentication counterpart to the identity-proofing evaluator (art-523), on the same framework-as-input pattern: the framework supplies levels ordered lowest-to-highest, each carrying criteria in a shared generic vocabulary (a distinct-factor-category floor, required factor categories, phishing-resistance / verifier-impersonation-resistance / hardware-binding / dynamic-authentication requirements, reauthentication and idle-timeout ceilings in minutes, and restricted authenticator kinds). The kernel never interprets a framework it was not given: every threshold and restriction comes from the declared framework, and authenticator kinds come from the node's own closed enum (password, otp_device, otp_sms, crypto_software, crypto_hardware, passkey_synced, passkey_device_bound, biometric_local), with factor categories only ever tested for set membership in the caller's own vocabulary. A criterion whose declared value is malformed is flagged AAL_DEFINITION_INSUFFICIENT -- the definition cannot express what it asks for -- which is distinct from AAL_SHORTFALL (declared data failing a well-formed criterion, reported per criterion as {criterion, required, found}); the two are never conflated. When the target level is not met, achieved_level falls back to the highest fully-met level below it. The named compliance flags cover a restricted authenticator in use, missing phishing resistance, an exceeded reauthentication interval, and a short factor count. Honest posture: this evidences that a declared authenticator set was measured against a declared policy. It does not assert anyone controls any authenticator, does not verify possession, biometrics or device state, and carries no user identifiers -- inputs are kinds, boolean capabilities and minute intervals, nothing else. The shipped example frameworks in its fixtures are modeled on NIST SP 800-63B-4 AAL1-3 and on the authentication section of the eIDAS implementing regulation's annex; both are caller data, and no output implies endorsement by NIST, the European Commission or any government.
